sections.overview: Peribatodes ilicaria is a geometrid moth found in Europe; in Britain it is a rare migrant, while it is established in parts of continental Europe.
sections.identification: It is similar to the Willow Beauty, P. rhomboidaria, but usually has heavier, more distinct speckling.
sections.habitat: It favors warm, dry wooded places and scrub; in France it is more frequent in the Centre and South than in the North.
sections.diet: Its caterpillars feed on a range of trees and shrubs, with French accounts noting lichens and records from oak, holly, juniper and pine.
sections.behavior: Adults fly mainly in summer; British records are too few to define a reliable flight period there.
sections.reproduction: It usually has one generation per year, and the caterpillar overwinters; a second spring generation is reported exceptionally in southern France.
sections.ecology: The Willow Beauty is its close congener and a useful identification comparison, but the two remain separate species with different reported patterns.
sections.conservation: A 2022 Île-de-France survey calls its regional status threatened. A separate French data portal says it has no Red List assessment, so these local sources do not establish a global category.
